I speak the truth and do not lie, I did not receive from another if not from the eternal king Jesus Christ. Herod said: 'Who clothed you in this garment?' The holy Longinus said: 'He himself sent his angel and clothed me in this garment and sealed me with the seal of the eternal king Jesus Christ.' Herod said to his magistrates: 'Since he lies, thinking he received from his king, take the garment from him and burn it with fire.' The magistrates approached to do what was commanded, but found nothing to take or remove from him. The magistrates said to the king: 'Behold, we see him clothed in a shadow, and we cannot take anything from him.' Herod said: 'Now I know that there is magic in making the cloak invisible.' The holy Longinus said: 'By the heavenly king who came down from heaven, I do not know what magic is; for he himself hates magicians and sorcerers. How can I, being his servant, have a heart polluted with magic and deceit? But I tell you that the power of God has surrounded me and protects me.' Herod, troubled by Longinus' responses, ordered his soldiers to pierce him.

Now I am relieved, having suffered for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, having become his friend and being loved by him. For I was held in great fear because of your evil deeds. Herod, gnashing his teeth at Longinus, says to his magistrates: 'Having struck Longinus, the ungodly soldier, with three blows of wood, put heavy iron on him, so that, being melted and torn apart, he may lose his strength and beauty, and all people who know him may see him and lament.' And they did what they were ordered to do. After thirty days, with the chains weighing lightly on him, Herod again sought the holy Longinus, saying to his magistrates: 'Bring me the prisoner Longinus to the tribunal, so that, seeing him gloomy and disfigured, I may be relieved.' The magistrates, having come to the prison and seen his face shining, were afraid to bring him to the tribunal. Nevertheless, taking him because of Herod's order, they brought the beautiful athlete of Christ to the tribunal. Herod, having seen his face like the face of an angel, gnashed his teeth at his magistrates, tore his clothes, and said: 'Instead of punishments, bring me this prisoner.' And Herod, being furious at his magistrates, expelled them.
pass_b_english: Herod was furious and ordered that the man be thrown into the inner prison, with a golden necklace around his neck and heavy chains placed around his neck and waist, until he could devise many torments for him. After that, he would have the man's head cut off. He then issued a decree that all infants in Bethlehem, from two years old and under, were to be killed. The soldiers carried out the king's orders and slaughtered all the infants.

Herod's rage was fueled by his deception at the hands of the Magi, and he summoned Longinus, ordering him to be brought before him. When Longinus was led in, the king noticed that he was wearing a golden necklace around his neck, a royal cloak, and a sword at his waist. Herod was enraged and roared like a lion, demanding to know why his nobles had not removed the necklace, sword, and cloak. The nobles replied that they had followed the king's orders, but they did not know who had dressed Longinus in the royal attire. Herod then turned to Longinus and demanded that he confess who had given him the royal clothes.

I speak the truth and do not lie, for I have received my testimony from none other than the eternal King Jesus Christ himself. Herod, however, was skeptical and asked, 'Who is it that has clothed you in this garment?' The holy Longinus replied, 'It was the Lord himself who sent his angel to clothe me in this garment and to seal me with the seal of the eternal King Jesus Christ.'

Herod, unconvinced by Longinus' words, ordered his magistrates to take the garment from him and burn it with fire, believing that Longinus was lying about receiving it from his king. But when the magistrates approached Longinus, they found that they could not take the garment from him, for it seemed to be surrounded by a shadow. They reported back to Herod, saying, 'We see him clothed in a shadow, and we cannot take anything from him.' Herod, realizing that there was something supernatural at work, exclaimed, 'Now I know that there is magic in making the cloak invisible.' The holy Longinus, however, denied any knowledge of magic, saying, 'By the heavenly King who came down from heaven, I do not know what magic is, for he himself hates magicians and sorcerers. How can I, being his servant, have a heart polluted with magic and deceit? But I tell you that the power of God has surrounded me and protects me.' Herod, troubled by Longinus' responses, ordered his soldiers to pierce him.
Now I am relieved, having suffered for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, having become his friend and being loved by him. For I was held in great fear because of your evil machinations.

Herod, however, was not so easily swayed, and his anger towards Longinus, the ungodly soldier, only intensified. He ordered his magistrates to strike Longinus with three blows of wood and to put heavy iron on him, so that, being melted and torn apart, he may lose his strength and beauty. But despite the brutal treatment, Longinus remained unbroken, and his face continued to shine as if it were the face of an angel. When Herod saw him, he was furious, and his anger was directed not only at Longinus but also at his own magistrates, whom he expelled in a fit of rage.
